gaps.missing: the generic-substitution mirror diverged from the judge on the NULLABLE spelling of a type variable: hasTypeVar split the signature on `,` and required the whole token to be one capital letter, so `(T?)` — how Kotlin writes every generic parameter — read as a CONCRETE type. The exact-signature test then failed AND the documented name-only fallback never fired, so an override whose DECLARING ancestor is a GRANDPARENT interface fell through to the first-supertype guess. Measured on exposed-core ColumnType.kt (`ColumnWithTransform : ColumnType`, `ColumnType : IColumnType`, `IColumnType.valueToDB sig=(T?)`): the analyzer published `ColumnType.valueToDB` at 0.5 — a type that declares no such member — where the truth says `IColumnType.valueToDB`. Four such rows, and they were the oracle-sharpness sweep's first HARD masks on a lane other than groovy (#949).
gaps.closure: CLOSED — the mirror is now boundary-for-boundary the judge's `hasTypeVar` (kotlinSigHasTypeVar, char-scan), so `(T?)` is a type variable while `(Byte?)`/`(Wrapped?)` stay concrete and the exact-signature overload guard is intact. Evidence: (1) fixture kotlin/override-declaring-ancestor-949, whose in-place revert of the mirror fails exactly 4 of its assertions (2 expects at 0.9 naming IRenderer + 2 forbid entries naming the dangling `Base.render`@0.5) while the boundary row still passes — the fixture is falsified in the pre-fix state, not merely green in the fixed one; (2) mutant kotlin/override-grandparent-ancestor-revert CAUGHT by that fixture ALONE, derived from the result (the source owner's own first extends/implements target) rather than a hardcoded string; (3) the full-extent lane re-measured (Exposed 19,958 truth rows, kotlinx-coroutines 18,327 truth rows): strict-missing 0, hidden 0, hard 0, soft 0 — the four masks gone at the same 38,285 truth rows the pre-fix run reported, so the truth set did not move.

decisions.question: companion object {} is anonymous (no name); contents emit with owner = enclosing class (probe-verified). Recommend: declared limitation — no symbol for the anonymous companion itself.
decisions.resolution: DECLARED LIMITATION: companion object {} is anonymous (no name); contents emit with owner = the enclosing class (probe-verified, 2026-08-27). Companion members are the class's static surface, so the attribution is semantically correct; no symbol for the anonymous companion itself.

decisions.node_type: enum class supertype heritage (enum class MODE(...) : ForUpdateOrShareMode)
decisions.question: M37.21 #610 kotlin calls-oracle wave: extractEnumClass never extracted superTypes, so every enum-with-supertype silently dropped its heritage (measured: Exposed ForUpdateOption.kt MODE -> ForUpdateOrShareMode MISSING at 200-file depth).
decisions.resolution: extractEnumClass now extracts superTypes/superTypesAreConstructorCalls like extractClass/extractObject; the heritage post-pass admits SymbolKind.Enum alongside Class/Interface with unchanged Kotlin semantics (constructor-invocation supertype = extends, bare = implements). Both kotlin lanes 100%/0/0 at 200 files; fixture kotlin/enum-supertype-heritage pins implements Direction->Mode + extends Counted->Numbered; mutant kotlin/enum-supertype-drop.

decisions.question: M37.21 #610 master-review finding: kotlin (like all JVM languages) had NO dedicated calls oracle — the generic deriveTreeEdges audited heritage/instantiates/overrides only, so the entire call surface was never compared (truth 218 -> 5078 edges on Exposed at 200 files).
decisions.resolution: deriveKotlinEdges mirrors RealKotlinAnalyzer's call contract exactly: buildKotlinCallExpression receiver.selector chains (direct navigation_expression child only — ERROR-recovered comment-wrapped chains must never recurse, the analyzer reads the direct callee path), leaf extraction, stdlib exclusion (prefixes + exact sets), the MEASURED PascalCase construction rule (bare PascalCase = instantiates, qualified = calls), and constructor_delegation_call super/this. Exposed + kotlinx-coroutines 100%/0/0 at 200 files.

decisions.node_type: override fun m() in a class whose supertype declares m in the same file (K2/K34/K4 cluster)
decisions.question: Review K2: overrides carried no signature and every override was a first-parent guess at 0.5 even when the declaring parent was IN THIS FILE (weakest override machinery in the JVM family). What is the verification contract?
decisions.decision: In-file BFS verification (family convention: java JD-anon / scala waves): hoist a name-keyed declSigs index (owner -> method name -> Set<(T1,T2)>) ONCE (O(M), java C11 lesson). The FIRST ancestor in declaration order that declared a method WITH THE SAME NAME and a compatible signature verifies the edge at 0.9 / structural / reasonCode in-file-verified. The NAME dimension is load-bearing: name-blind sig membership fabricated cross-member overrides on the corpus (kotlinx-coroutines BroadcastChannel.kt: SubBroadcastChannel.send verified against BroadcastChannel which declares only cancel/sendSuspend - send comes from external SendChannel; 8 fabricated 0.9 edges at @200). Generic-substituted sigs (type-variable tokens) fall back to name-only pairing (scala SCD-E ruling). Parents that never declared the method keep the honest guess: 0.5 / inferred / first-supertype-guess (M37.10 family convention, below the 0.7 consumer threshold - K34 pin).

decisions.question: Review K4: override edges carry no signature, so overloads collapse and downstream cannot distinguish targets. Should the signature live in the edge source?
decisions.decision: Family convention (scala L433 / java C3): override sources stay Owner.name -> Parent.name - NO signature in the source string. The signature rides in metadata.overrideSig as a normalized '(T1,T2)' parameter-type list. Pinned by override-fallback-confidence (meta.overrideSig='()' + a forbid asserting the sig never leaks into the source) and the K4 claim-probe re-pin. Regression mutants: override-verification-downgrade (guess tier) and override-sig-payload-drop (payload loss) both die on the fixture.

decisions.question: Review K6/K23: performKotlinTypeInference gated on SymbolKind.Variable but the extractor emits Property - every branch unreachable. Feed it locals or delete it?
decisions.decision: DELETED as dishonest. The branches inferred types from NAME PREFIXES (is/has->Boolean, remember/mutableStateOf->MutableState) - guessing masquerading as inference. Local var symbols are intentionally NOT emitted (family convention: java emits their TYPE references, not Variable-kind symbols; locals are not project-symbol-table members - K23 probe re-pin). metadata.hasTypeInference stays (declared-type extraction IS real inference input).

decisions.question: Review K8/K9: routes only read value=, fell back to regexes for paths, and defaulted every mapping to GET, ignoring (method = RequestMethod.POST).
decisions.decision: Uniform named-argument walker over the annotation's value_argument list (value | path | method keys, nested value_arguments), replacing both regexes - a char-range leaf fallback keeps the R2 no-regex census contract. method=RequestMethod.X parses the accessor chain; unknown/missing method stays undefined rather than fabricating GET. Route = basePath + path (array values joined). Probe: (path = ['/x'], method = POST) -> apiContractPath=/x.

decisions.question: Review K10: patterns matched raw identifier text (let/apply/map on ANY node), so comments and member names ('this is a test', letIt) fabricated Smart Casts / Higher-Order Functions patterns.
decisions.decision: AST-gated: Smart Casts requires a check_expression node (is/!is); Higher-Order Functions requires lambda_literal/function_type/anonymous_function nodes; Elvis/Scope functions require elvis_expression / quest-bearing navigation nodes. Comment text is excluded (comments are skipped by the walker). Probe pins: '// this is a test' no longer triggers Smart Casts; fun letIt() no longer triggers Higher-Order Functions.

decisions.node_type: constructor symbols and ctor call sources (K11)
decisions.question: Review K11: every ctor symbol was named 'constructor' (all classes collide; contains: A->constructor, B->constructor indistinguishable) and ctor call sources said 'constructor'.
decisions.decision: Family convention (java C3, verified probe): ctor symbols are named after their CLASS; ctor call sources resolve to the class name (both extractKotlinCalls and collectExpressionUses). Self-contains edges (A->A) are family-normal (java emits them post-C3). Kotlin lanes compare overrides target-only so the contains self-edge never hits truth.

decisions.question: Review K13/K14: countMethods walked entire ASTs (O(N) per symbol, N^2 total), and enum members/lambda-local vals attributed to the wrong scope.
decisions.decision: Direct-children membership only, scoped to class_body AND enum_class_body (probe: enum members live in enum_class_body). Dead helpers deleted (findCompanionObject, extractDefaultArgs, performKotlinTypeInference); countMethods O(N) total.

decisions.question: Review K15: the typeIndex loop declared `let i` but never used it, and the override loop re-scanned symbols per iteration.
decisions.decision: Cleanup: dead loop variable removed; declSigs hoisted (KD21) so the override pass is O(M) after O(M) index build. Verified: typecheck clean, corpus perf unchanged (3285 edges @200 files, comparable runtimes).

decisions.question: Which spellings of a parameter type count as a TYPE VARIABLE for the generic-substitution fallback, given that the judge's rule (differential hasTypeVar, sigCompatible) and the analyzer's mirror must agree or the differential stops measuring one question?
decisions.decision: MIRROR THE JUDGE, BOUNDARY FOR BOUNDARY (the java #904 and scala S1.17 convention): a type variable is a SINGLE capital at `(`, `,`, `:`, `|`, `[`, `<`, `&` or string start — so `(T?)` is generic, and `(Byte?)`/`(Wrapped?)` are concrete. The nullable marker is stripped by the SCAN (the identifier ends at `?`), never by a per-token rule that would also make a nullable concrete type generic; the judge cannot derive an edge it reads as concrete, so widening past it fabricates UNEXPLAINED rows instead of fixing them. `kotlinSigHasTypeVar` is the third module-local copy of this scan (java javaSigHasTypeVar, scala sigHasTypeVar); consolidation into one shared mirror is a candidate, deliberately NOT taken in this round because two of the three lanes' rows are certified against their current bytes.

decisions.question: The F8 census injects ERROR and MISSING into every language's node-type set by hand (they are not in the wasm symbol table), yet no kotlin spec row claimed them, so section-a failed for kotlin on the same pair that fails lanes everywhere. Gap, silent omission, or handled?
decisions.decision: RULED — HANDLED, following the precedent the gate itself names and the java lane's own ruling (JDJ-2). The analyzer holds an EXPLICIT guard at real-kotlin-analyzer.ts:153 — `if (node.type === "ERROR" || node.type === "MISSING")` — which records a diagnostic and bypasses the damaged subtree. So ERROR is handled_verified and MISSING is internal_silent, the same split java, bash and javascript use. The guard being present is what makes the row CORRECT rather than grammar drift: a spec that classifies a node the analyzer consults was being told its own row was wrong, and the fix is never to delete the correct row.
decisions.evidence: Probed on the pinned grammar, 7 malformed inputs: `class E { class Inner { val w = 1 }` (unterminated class), `class F { val a = 1` (unterminated brace), `class H { val a = 1 } }` (stray close brace), `fun f(` (truncated parameter list), `val x =` (lone operator), `class I<T extends> { val a: List<,> }` (malformed generics), and a well-typed class with one bad method. Result in EVERY case: exactly 1 ERROR node, 0 MISSING nodes, hasError=true, and exactly 1 diagnostic ("Syntax ERROR detected. The Brain Engine is bypassing this broken node."). Partial extraction is preserved where the grammar recovered it — symbols were [w], [a], [H,a], [], [], [I,a], [ok] — so the guard bypasses the damaged node and not the file.
decisions.misssing_note: MISSING is internal_silent on a stronger ground than java's: the pinned kotlin grammar did not produce a single MISSING node across all 7 probes — it recovers to an ERROR node in every case — so the MISSING branch of the guard is unexercisable on this grammar rather than merely unexercised. The row is kept because the guard tests for it, and a guard branch that cannot currently be reached is still a statement about the analyzer's contract.

decisions.question: The override resolver has three passes: an in-file BFS that verifies the declarer by signature (0.9, in-file-verified), a companion-index variant of the same BFS (0.9, companion-index), and a fallback that names the FIRST SUPERTYPE at confidence 0.5 with reasonCode first-supertype-guess and evidenceClass inferred. Pass 3 fires when the declaring ancestor lives in another compilation unit and is therefore unknowable from this file alone. The justification in the code is that 0.5 sits BELOW THE CONSUMER THRESHOLD, so those rows read as declared suspicion rather than counted relationships. Is that justification sufficient, and what is the tier's actual error rate?
decisions.decision: RULED — the tier STAYS, and its justification is REPLACED by a measurement. Same ruling and same shape as java's JDJ-1, reached the same way: the reasoning was true but unquantified, which is not the same as verified. Measured on Exposed (250-file draw, every edge checked against a repo-wide index of types and their declared members built from all 791 .kt files): guess tier 302 edges — 105 correct, 197 WRONG = 65.2%; verified tier 103 edges — 103 correct, 0 wrong = 0.0%. Kotlin's guess tier is more than twice java's measured 30.6%.
decisions.why_it_stays: It is right about a third of the time, so suppressing it would delete 105 correct edges. Deleting a correct edge to avoid 197 wrong ones, at a confidence the code already labels `inferred` and carries a `reasonCode` for, is a worse trade than publishing both honestly — the consumer's decision to filter is better made by the consumer than made silently here.
decisions.what_the_measurement_changes: The JUSTIFICATION, which does not hold as written. The 0.7 `confidenceThreshold` in src/ast/patterns.ts is the default for ORPHANED-PATTERN DETECTION, not a filter on the relationship ingest path, and no confidence predicate was found on that path. So the tier's defensibility does not rest on a filter that might not exist; it rests on `reasonCode: first-supertype-guess` and `evidenceClass: inferred` being present on every row. That is why kotlin/override-guess-tier pins both rather than leaving them implied — a consumer must be able to distinguish a guess from a verified edge without hard-coding 0.5 as a magic number. Stated as unverified rather than refuted: the insert path was not located, so the claim that no filter exists is the absence of evidence found, not proof of absence.
decisions.comparability: Kotlin's 65.2% and java's 30.6% are NOT the same measurement. Java's denominator excluded 33 unverifiable guesses whose claimed owner was itself outside the repo, and reported 30.6% of the VERIFIABLE subset. This measurement has no unverifiable bucket: every claimed parent resolved to a type in the repo, and 0 were 'not a type at all'. So the two figures answer different questions and the difference is not only that kotlin is worse.
decisions.measurement_instrument: Three instrument versions, each of which produced a confidently wrong rate, and the sequence is the finding as much as the number: 79.1% when the index missed constructor-invocation supertypes (the dominant kotlin form, `class Column<T>(...) : ExpressionWithColumnType<T>()` — it found 2 of Column's 3); 66.2% when it also missed anonymous objects as types, so every anonymous_LazySizedIterable.* edge resolved to no hierarchy and scored wrong; 65.2% with the instrument validated. A rate is only as good as what the instrument can see, and an unvalidated instrument does not report uncertainty — it reports a number.
decisions.fixture: kotlin/override-guess-tier — 2 expects, 2 forbids. Disabling pass 3 fails the guess row. Disabling pass 1 does NOT remove the verified row: it SILENTLY DEMOTES it from 0.9/in-file-verified/structural to 0.5/first-supertype-guess/inferred, and the edge's presence is unchanged. That is the most dangerous available failure mode for this rule — a count-based check, a coverage number, and an existence assertion all pass — and it is why the fixture pins confidence, reasonCode and evidenceClass together. The forbids are the second load-bearing half: without the `override` modifier neither tier may fire, because guessing there fabricates an override that is really an overload.
